status_summary: On 2025-08-06 VA announced it was ending collective bargaining agreements for most bargaining-unit employees represented by five unions, citing Executive Order 14251, which added VA to the agencies excluded from federal labor-management relations programs; contracts for about 4,000 police officers, firefighters and security guards were kept. A federal district court in Rhode Island issued a preliminary injunction on 2026-03-13 requiring VA to reinstate its contract with AFGE. Reporting says a First Circuit panel in May 2026 denied VA's motion to stay that injunction, and on 2026-08-07 the district court granted a motion to enforce it after VA gave notice in July 2026 of a new termination effective 2026-08-08.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14251 signed, excluding certain agencies, including VA, from federal labor-management relations programs.
VA announced it had ended collective bargaining agreements for most bargaining-unit employees, keeping contracts for about 4,000 police, firefighters and security guards.
The U.S. District Court in Rhode Island issued a preliminary injunction requiring VA to reinstate its contract with AFGE.
The court granted a motion to enforce the injunction, rejecting VA's July 2026 notice of re-termination effective 2026-08-08; reporting said the contract remains in effect.
